title: Whether & I Wonder: かどうか, かな, かしら, じゃないか, かい
description: Embedded yes/no questions with かどうか, wondering with かな/かしら, 'isn't it!' with じゃないか, and casual questions with かい.

points.title: 〜かどうか: whether or not
points.summary: Plain form + かどうか embeds a YES/NO question. With a question word (何, いつ, どこ…) use just か. Nouns / な-adj attach directly.
points.body:
**Yes/no question inside a sentence:**
- 彼が来る**かどうか**わかりません (I don't know whether he'll come).
- 明日休み**かどうか**知っていますか (do you know whether tomorrow is a day off?).

**With a question word → only か:**
- 何時に来る**か**教えてください (✗ 何時に来るかどうか).

**Attachment:** plain form; nouns and な-adjectives **without だ**: 休み**かどうか**, 静か**かどうか**.

Typical verbs after it: わからない, 知らない, 聞く, 調べる, 確認する, 教える.
examples: {彼|かれ}が{来|く}るかどうかわかりません。
I don't know whether he'll come.
{何時|なんじ}に{来|く}るか{教|おし}えてください。
Please tell me what time you'll come.

points.title: 〜かな: I wonder
points.summary: Plain form + かな = wondering aloud / to yourself. Casual. Nouns and な-adj attach directly (雨かな).
points.body:
- 明日、晴れる**かな** (I wonder if it'll be sunny tomorrow).
- これ、おいしい**かな** (I wonder if this is tasty).
- 明日は雨**かな** (no だ).

Variants: 〜かなあ (more drawn out), 〜**かな**と思う (I wonder…, I'm thinking maybe…).

Also used softly when asking for something: 手伝ってくれない**かな** (could you maybe help me?).

Used by everyone, but it's casual — in polite speech: 〜でしょうか.
examples: {明日|あした}、{晴|は}れるかな。
I wonder if it'll be sunny tomorrow.
{明日|あした}は{雨|あめ}かな。
I wonder if it'll rain tomorrow.

points.title: 〜かしら: I wonder (feminine)
points.summary: Same meaning as かな, traditionally used by women (and in older or very polite speech).
points.body:
- 田中さん、もう来た**かしら** (I wonder if Tanaka has come already).
- これ、似合う**かしら** (I wonder if this suits me).

It sounds feminine and somewhat old-fashioned; younger speakers of all genders mostly use かな. You'll meet it a lot in novels, drama and anime.
examples: {田中|たなか}さん、もう{来|き}たかしら。
I wonder if Tanaka has arrived yet.
このスカート、{似合|にあ}うかしら。
I wonder if this skirt suits me.

points.title: 〜じゃないか: isn't it! / hey, it's …!
points.summary: Not a real question: じゃないか expresses surprise, discovery or emphasis ('That's great!', 'Hey, it's you!'). Formal: ではないか.
points.body:
Despite the negative form, it's a **positive exclamation**:
- すごい**じゃないか**！ (That's amazing!)
- 田中さん**じゃないか**！久しぶり！ (Hey, if it isn't Tanaka!)
- だから言った**じゃないか** (I told you so, didn't I!)

Variants: じゃない (casual, often rising), じゃないですか (polite), ではないか (written/formal).

It attaches to plain forms; nouns and な-adjectives directly (田中さんじゃないか, 元気じゃないか).
examples: {田中|たなか}さんじゃないか！{久|ひさ}しぶり！
Hey, it's Tanaka! Long time no see!
すごいじゃないか！
That's amazing!

points.title: 〜かい / 〜だい: casual question (male, friendly)
points.summary: Plain form + かい = casual yes/no question (often older/male, friendly). With a question word, use だい instead.
points.body:
- 元気**かい**？ (You doing well?)
- もう寝る**かい**？ (Going to bed already?)

**Yes/no → かい; question word → だい:**
- どこへ行くん**だい**？ (✗ どこへ行くかい)
- 何を食べたん**だい**？

It sounds warm and a bit old-fashioned or masculine (a father to a child, an older man to a younger person).
examples: {元気|げんき}かい？
You doing well?
どこへ{行|い}くんだい？
Where are you going?

questions.prompt: {彼|かれ}がパーティーに{来|く}る（　）わかりません。
notes: かとうか isn't a form (どう, not とう).
かどうが isn't a form.
かどか isn't a form.
questions.translation: I don't know whether he'll come to the party.

questions.prompt: {明日|あした}が{休|やす}み（　）{知|し}っていますか。
notes: 休みのかどうか isn't grammatical (it would need なの: 休みなのかどうか).
な isn't used with nouns here.
だ disappears before かどうか.
questions.translation: Do you know whether tomorrow is a day off?

questions.prompt: {何時|なんじ}に{来|く}る（　）{教|おし}えてください。
questions.explanation: With a **question word** (何時), use only **か**.
notes: かは doesn't fit before 教える here.
かどうか is only for yes/no questions — not with 何時.
かどうが isn't a form.
questions.translation: Please tell me what time you'll come.

questions.prompt: （Talking to yourself）{明日|あした}は{雨|あめ}（　）。
notes: な isn't used with nouns.
だ disappears before かな.
雨のかな isn't grammatical (雨なのかな would be).
questions.translation: I wonder if it'll rain tomorrow.

questions.prompt: In which situation would you say 「おいしいかな」?
options: Telling a customer the food is delicious
Asking a teacher politely if the food is good
Wondering aloud whether something will taste good
Complaining that the food was bad
notes: That would be おいしいですよ.
Politely you'd say おいしいでしょうか.
That would be おいしくなかった.

questions.explanation: **かしら** is traditionally used by women.
notes: かな is used by everyone.
ぜ is a rough masculine sentence ending.
だろう is plain 'probably' (often male in conversation).

questions.prompt: {田中|たなか}さん、もう{来|き}た（　）。
notes: からし means 'mustard'.
かしれ isn't a sentence ending (it's part of かもしれない).
かしり isn't a word.
questions.translation: I wonder if Tanaka has arrived yet.

questions.prompt: あれ、{田中|たなか}さん（　）！{久|ひさ}しぶり！
notes: じゃいないか isn't a form.
じゃないが means 'isn't, but…'.
じゃなかか isn't a form.
questions.translation: Hey, it's Tanaka! Long time no see!

questions.prompt: What does 「すごいじゃないか！」 mean?
questions.explanation: じゃないか is an **exclamation**, not a negative.
notes: That would be すごいですか.
That would be すごいかもしれない.
That would be すごくない.
がい isn't a question ending.
かえ is dialectal/archaic, not standard.
かや isn't a standard ending.

questions.explanation: かい is for **yes/no** questions; with a question word you need **だい** (どこへ行くんだい).
notes: With 何, use だい: 何を食べるんだい？
With だれ, use だい: だれが来たんだい？
With どこ, use だい: どこへ行くんだい？
